# Retro — Markdown export and note tags in the notes CLI

- **Change:** /path/to/project/docs/changes/2026-10-16-change-b · **Commits:** 1a2b3c4^1..1a2b3c4, 2b3c4d5^1..2b3c4d5, 3c4d5e6^1..3c4d5e6, 4d5e6f7^1..4d5e6f7, 5e6f7a8^1..5e6f7a8, 6f7a8b9^1..6f7a8b9
- **Models:** prepass: haiku · reader: sonnet · retro: opus
- **Versions:** kentra-rpir 0.4.0 · Claude Code 2.1.301 · skills —
## Findings

| Id | Class | Finding | Decisive step | How it made sense at the time | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | PLAN | M2 told the implementer to generate the golden files for `notes export` by running the CLI on the host. It left PL4 ("export output does not depend on the machine's timezone") unverified, and its contract check ran only on the host. The golden files hold the created-at stamps rendered in the host's local zone, so the CI job, which runs in UTC, fails 9 of 31 export tests. Nobody saw this until the CI run after all 6 milestones had merged. It cost a plan amendment (8e9f0a1), a fix dispatch and a second verify round. | plan.yaml (pre-8e9f0a1):2210 "PL4 \| normal \| unverified \| — \| ... export renders the same text on any machine" | The plan's step 4 and its check (`make test`) never mention the CI workflow or the timezone. To the plan author, golden files generated and then compared on the same host looked like enough proof. The implementer followed it exactly: "Golden files regenerated as the plan describes" (<transcript>:52). | high |
| F2 | PROCESS | The first M2 verifier only reran the implementer's host-only check, so its PASS on the golden files was a lucky pass. The workflow file the implementer printed shows a CI job that sets no TZ variable. The second environment was visible in context, but no verification step required running the tests under it. | <transcript>:49 (verifier PASS rerunning the same host check) | The verifier's job was framed as checking the contract. The contract check passed with 31/31, and nothing in the dispatch named CI as a second reader of the golden files. The `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` line at <transcript>:27 appeared only as incidental output. | medium |
| F3 | SKILL | Because the change was light tier, tool-behaviour premises were deferred to implementation and never researched. PL4 was refuted in implement. Others stayed unverified in a 2.1k-line plan (PL2 Markdown escaping of pipe characters in table cells, PL5 whether `--since` accepts "yesterday", PL6 how the search index tokenizes hyphenated words). Meanwhile, planning effort went into repeated full reviews. | <transcript>:480 "These stay unresearched because this is a light-tier plan" | The agent applied the tier rule as it read it: light tier allows deferring research. It spent its verification budget on skeleton and full reviews, which do not run tools. | medium |
| F4 | SPEC | The agreed spec carried an old-format placeholder into the new export: a note without a title was written with the literal title "untitled". This was challenged only at plan review. The user's decision (a title is optional, and the export omits the heading) forced a spec amendment, a re-skeleton, new milestone writers and a second full plan review. It also refuted PL8 (every exported file has a heading). | <transcript>:402 "The export wrote the word 'untitled' for notes with no title. I treated the old format's placeholder as data, and I shouldn't have." | A missing title looks like a gap to fill. Writing the same placeholder the plain-text listing used seemed a faithful, mechanical translation. | high |
| F5 | SPEC | The spec stage never asked how notebooks should be modelled, even though export has to walk them. The user's layout (notebooks as subfolders, one level deep, with a shared `_inbox`) came out only when the export milestone met a `--all` flag. That turned a single-folder export into a multi-notebook one: 64 added spec lines, 9 question rounds and one new milestone (notebook-walk). | <transcript>:301 "Just export my notes to Markdown files, one per note." | The request was worded as a single-folder export. The spec-stage exploration mapped the command's inputs, not where notes can live, so a flat notes directory looked within scope. | high |

## Actions

| Finding | Action | Target | Detail | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | automated check | /path/to/project/notes-cli/Makefile (+ notes-cli/tests/conftest.py) | Pin the timezone the tests run under, so a host-specific zone can no longer leak into golden files that CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) compares. Export `TZ=UTC` in the Makefile's `test` target and set `os.environ["TZ"] = "UTC"` plus `time.tzset()` in conftest.py. Golden files are then regenerated under UTC, which is what fix 9f0a1b2 did by hand after plan amendment 8e9f0a1. Pass: `TZ=Pacific/Auckland make test` exits 0 on the host, and the CI job passes. | Apply: a0b1c2d on main |
| F2 | diff | kentra-io/kentra-rpir: agents/verifier.md | BEFORE (after item 5): no item. AFTER: add item "6. **Other readers.** When the diff changes output that a second environment compares (golden files, snapshots, generated docs), run the check under that environment's settings too, e.g. `TZ=UTC make test`, even when the contract's check does not. Report its result on the CHECK line." Removes nothing and adds three lines. It pays for itself because the M2 verifier passed on a rerun of the host-only check (<transcript>:49), even though the workflow file it had in context showed a CI job with no timezone set (<transcript>:27). Running under UTC at M2 would have caught the failures before 6 merges instead of after them, which would have saved plan amendment 8e9f0a1, a fix dispatch and a second verify round. | Reject (user gave no reason) |
| F3 | diff | kentra-io/kentra-rpir: skills/plan/SKILL.md | Tier table, Research row, `light` column. BEFORE: "`critical` claims only; `normal` ones stay `unverified`". AFTER: "`critical` claims, plus any claim about a tool's behaviour that one local command settles (run it the way the plan's check will, and record the output); other `normal` ones stay `unverified`". This replaces the existing cell, so it adds about one line. It pays for itself because PL4 (export output independent of timezone) would have taken one `TZ=UTC` run, but it was deferred under "These stay unresearched because this is a light-tier plan" (<transcript>:480) and then refuted in implement. That cost 8e9f0a1, 9f0a1b2 and a second verify round, while PL2 (pipes in table cells), PL5 (`--since yesterday`) and PL6 (hyphen tokenizing) stayed unverified. | Reject (user gave no reason) |
| F4 | diff | kentra-io/kentra-rpir: skills/spec/SKILL.md | Step 3 Ask: add one bullet. BEFORE: (none). AFTER: "- For a new output format derived from an existing one, list each placeholder or default the source format shows (an 'untitled' label, a zero date, a blank field) and ask whether the target keeps it. Do not carry one over as a mechanical translation." Adds two lines. It pays for itself because the 'untitled' carry-over (<transcript>:402) was challenged only at plan review. The user's decision then forced spec amendment b1c2d3e, a re-skeleton, a second plan-milestones run (~0.5M tokens) and a second full plan review (~0.6M tokens), and it refuted PL8. | Reject (user gave no reason) |
| F5 | eval case | kentra-io/kentra-rpir: skills/spec/SKILL.md | Prompt: "/kentra-rpir:spec Add a `notes export` command that writes my notes as Markdown files." Fixture commit: c2d3e4f in the example project (the parent of spec commit d3e4f5a). Simulated user: answers questions using the notebook layout described in a notes file, and volunteers nothing unasked. Pass: before the spec reaches `status: agreed`, the agent asks at least one question about where notes can live and how many notebooks exist (subfolders, an inbox, nesting), or it records that as a non-goal the user confirmed. Fail: the spec is agreed for a single flat folder and no such question. An eval rather than a diff, because "ask about the storage layout" does not generalise as prose. The eval measures whether the F4 bullet and the existing exploration step surface layout questions behind a request worded as a single-folder export. Here the question surfaced only at the `--all` flag and cost 64 spec lines, 9 question rounds and one extra milestone. | Reject (user gave no reason) |
| F7 | automated check | kentra-io/kentra-rpir: scripts/commit-change.sh | Add a guard before staging. When the change folder holds a `.reviewed` file, commit-change.sh compares its sha256 with the one of the document being committed and refuses a spec or plan commit whose hash differs, with the message: "edited after its last review; run a diff review". The self-review workflow writes `.reviewed` at the end of every full or diff review. That turns the existing table rule (an edit that changes step code needs a diff review) into a check, for the cases skipped here: the spec amendment, and the last plan fixes that changed counts and tests in a 2,140-line plan (<transcript>:510). Test: add a case under tests/ for the refusal. | File: https://github.com/kentra-io/kentra-rpir/issues/19 |
